([[Rancho Cucamonga, California]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2021–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 59 | draft_team = [[Houston Rockets]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team1 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team2 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team3 = →Memphis Hustle | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Defensive team (2025) }} '''Jahmai Hasan Mashack''' (born November 10, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]] and was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the last pick in the second round (59th) of the [[2025 NBA draft]]. ==Early life and high school career== Mashack was born on November 10, 2002, in [[Riverside, California]].{{Cite web |title=Jahmai Mashack |url=https://utsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jahmai-mashack/20401 |publisher=[[Tennessee Volunteers]]}} His father, Elton, was a first-team All-[[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) in [[basketball]] for the [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount Lions]], while his mother, Meika, competed in [[track and field]] for the [[UNLV Rebels track and field|UNLV Rebels]]. His older brother, Kwesi Mashack, played cornerback for the [[2014 Arizona Wildcats football team|Arizona Wildcats]] from 2014 to 2017. His younger sister, Malika Mashack, like her mother, is currently on the track & field team at UNLV Rebels.{{Cite web |last=Trotter, Isaac |date=February 17, 2025 |title=Tennessee's Jahmai Mashack chases Defensive Player of the Year while dad helps snuff California wildfires |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/tennessees-jahmai-mashack-chases-defensive-player-of-the-year-while-dad-helps-snuff-california-wildfires/ |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} At age four, he battled [[Guillain–Barré syndrome]], which he recovered from but required years of physical therapy. He attended [[Etiwanda High School]] in [[Rancho Cucamonga, California|Rancho Cucamonga]] and was a top basketball player there, excelling on defense.{{Cite news |last=Wilson, Mike |date=February 20, 2024 |title=Jahmai Mashack is a preparation junkie. Here's how the Tennessee basketball guard does it. |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2024/02/20/jahmai-mashack-defense-tennessee-basketball-film-study/72501736007/ |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250127234714/https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2024/02/20/jahmai-mashack-defense-tennessee-basketball-film-study/72501736007/ |archive-date=January 27, 2025 |access-date=July 15, 2025 |work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]] |via=[[archive.today]]}} He helped Etiwanda to the CIF Southern California Regional final as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] and as a [[Senior (education)|senior]] helped them to the title while being named the Cal-Hi Sports State Senior Player of the Year, the [[Baseline League]] Player of the Year and to the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' All-Star team. Ranked a four-star [[shooting guard]] prospect and a top-80 recruit nationally, he committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]]. ==College career== As a [[freshman]] for the Volunteers in 2021–22, Mashack appeared in 27 games while playing 4.6 minutes per game.{{Cite news |last=Wilson, Mike |date=November 22, 2022 |title=Jahmai Mashack accepted his role for Tennessee basketball. Now, he's owning it. |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2022/11/22/tennessee-basketball-jahmai-mashack-role-battle-4-atlantis-bahamas-tournament/69641827007/ |work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} He was part of the NCAA Tournament team as a freshman. The following year, he started 13 of 36 games and averaged 4.7 points.{{Cite news |last=Wilson, Mike |date=June 26, 2025 |title=Tennessee's Jahmai Mashack taken by Memphis Grizzlies with final pick of 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2025/06/26/jahmai-mashack-memphis-grizzlies-tennessee-basketball-nba-draft/84363411007/ |work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} He also started all three of Tennessee's NCAA Tournament games, averaging 6.7 points in those games. As a junior in 2023–24, Mashack averaged 4.5 points and 3.1 rebounds while starting eight games and contributing to the team's [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) regular season championship. In his last year, he started all 38 games and helped Tennessee reach the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament, averaging six points and 4.2 rebounds.{{Cite news |last=Smith, Lance |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Etiwanda alumni Jahmai Mashack picked by Memphis Grizzlies in second round of 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/high-school/boys-basketball/news/etiwanda-alumni-jahmai-mashack-picked-memphis-grizzlies-second-round-2025-nba-draft/b1fe16f4ce62fc614a4d1b41 |work=[[The Sporting News]]}} During his collegiate career, he won 109 games for the Volunteers, including nine in the NCAA Tournament, a team-record. Although Mashack averaged only 4.2 points per game during his four seasons at Tennessee, he was considered one of the top defensive players in the nation.{{Cite web |last=Issa, Matt |date=June 25, 2025 |title=NBA Draft 2025: Why You Can't Forget About Jahmai Mashack |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/matissa/2025/06/25/why-you-cant-forget-about-jahmai-mashack-this-draft-cycle/ |website=[[Forbes]]}} The ''[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]'' described him as a "master at knowing an opponent's strengths and weaknesses offensively" and he was often tasked with guarding opponents' best players.{{Cite news |last=Wilson, Mike |date=March 14, 2025 |title=Tennessee basketball's Jahmai Mashack felt disrespected. Texas' Tre Johnson paid the price |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2025/03/14/jahmai-mashack-tennessee-texas-basketball-sec-tournament-2025/81063301007/ |work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} In his last year, he ranked fourth nationally in [[Adjusted Plus Minus|Defensive Box Plus-Minus]] and was selected to the SEC All-Defensive team, as well as named a finalist for the [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award]]. In March 2025, he received Tennessee's Torchbearer award, the highest honor for school students. ==Professional career== Mashack was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the second round (59th overall) of the [[2025 NBA draft]], with his rights then traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] from the [[Golden State Warriors]] via the [[Phoenix Suns]], in a deal exchange for the draft rights to the 56th pick ([[Will Richard]]).{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2025 |title=Warriors Acquire Draft Rights To Forward Alex Toohey And Guard Jahmai Mashack |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-draft-rights-to-forward-alex-toohey-and-guard-jahmai-mashack-20250706 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2025 |title=Warriors Acquire Draft Rights To Guard Will Richard |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-draft-rights-to-guard-will-richard-20250706 |publisher=National Basketball Association |quote=The Golden State Warriors have acquired the draft rights to guard Will Richard, the 56th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, from the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for the draft rights to Jahmai Mashack, the 59th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, guard Justinian Jessup, the 51st overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft, and a future conditional second-round pick, it was announced Sunday.}} He was the final selection in the draft. Mashack and teammate [[Chaz Lanier]] were two players from the [[University of Tennessee]] to be drafted into the [[NBA]].{{cite web |title=Pistons Take Vols' Chaz Lanier Early in the Second Round|url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2025/jun/26/pistons-take-vols-chaz-lanier-early-in-the-second/ |website=[[Chattanooga Times Free Press]] |access-date=21 February 2026}} Mashack began the 2025–26 season on the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]]. On November 16, the Grizzlies signed Mashack to a [[two-way contract]].{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies Sign Jahmai Mashack to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jahmai-mashack-to-two-way-contract|access-date=November 30, 2025|publisher=National Basketball Association|language=en}} He made his NBA debut on November 20 against the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]], where he scored six points, and tallied up two rebounds in six minutes.{{Cite web |last=VolsWire Staff |title=Jahmai Mashack makes NBA debut with Memphis February 2026}} Mashack converted 3-of-9 field goal attempts and 2-of-7 three-point attempts.{{cite web |title=Former Vol makes first career NBA start |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/former-vol-makes-first-career-120544361.html |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |access-date=February 13, 2026 }} On February 9, Mashack scored a career-high 17 points against the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web |last=RotoWire Staff |title=Grizzlies' Jahmai Mashack starting Wednesday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-jahmai-mashack-starting-wednesday/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=February 13, 2026 }} On April 10, Mashack recorded a [[triple-double]] with 13 points, 15 rebounds, and 14 assists in a 147–101 loss to the [[2025–26 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]]. The performance marked as a career-high in rebounds and assists for Mashack.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-the-insane-triple-double-history-made-in-tank-off-vs-grizzlies|title=The insane triple-double history made in egregious tank-off Jazz vs. Grizzlies|website=[[ClutchPoints]]|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-jahmai-mashack-records-triple-double-in-rout/|title=Grizzlies' Jahmai Mashack: Records triple-double in rout|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}} Mashack finished the season averaging 6.2 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 2.2 assists. On June 30, 2026, it was announced that Mashack would be participating in the [[2026 NBA Summer League]] with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-announce-full-2026-summer-league-schedule|title=Memphis Grizzlies Announce Full 2026 Summer League Schedule|website=[[NBA.com]]|date=June 30, 2026|access-date=July 7, 2026}} ==Player profile== Mashack was widely regarded as one of the top defenders in college basketball during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]]. He is known for his aggressive, anticipatory style of defense and frequently takes on the opposing team's most challenging assignments, demonstrating activity with both his hands and feet. While he is most effective guarding guards and smaller wings, he is also capable of defending larger players due to his anticipation and physical strength. Offensively, Mashack is not expected to play a central role. He is considered a capable [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] shooter but does not pose a significant scoring threat, and his ball-handling and playmaking abilities are adequate.{{cite web |title=Jahmai Mashack – 2025 NBA Draft Prospect |url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2025/prospects/jahmai-mashack |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=21 February 2026}} ==Personal
